beforeafter-mapping-of-the-checks.text: The table maps every simulator control from what it observed before this slice to what it observes now. The new rows close the silent holes: an admitted case must show the modeled mint delta and the custody refund in both destination and amount, a guard fails if the corpus stops observing refunds at all, and every exported corpus section must be classified as behavior, evidence or uncovered. The replaced rows report honestly: theorem tables separate applicable, vacuous, held and exercised; receipts say inspected, never replayed; and naming rows are validated against the supply biconditional. Everything listed as preserved keeps its previous observation unchanged.

prepublication-repair-2026-09-21-full-s3.text: Two defects in the initial implementation were caught by prepublication owner checks and repaired against the Lean model. First, resolve rows could pass while contradicting the supply law, because the checker required one witness for the matching leaf but omitted the requirement for zero witnesses otherwise. It now requires both directions for active and absent witnesses, while still allowing plural terminal attestations. Second, the law gated itself on its own output, letting a violating state hide as an inactive hypothesis. The unconditional laws now apply to all ten accepted rows. On the preserved witness-dropping mutant, the report shows nine rows holding and one violating the supply and active-witness laws; the old report omitted that violation as vacuous.

verification-record.text: The record lists the commands and their results. The initial simulator baseline and candidate checks passed, and the prepublication repair used the final permitted simulator invocation successfully. The browser check used all three local invocations, failing once on a redundant label assertion and passing after the exact inspected wording was pinned. Red controls planted dropped mints, zeroed refunds and fabricated rows into the old checks and watched them survive. The strengthened gate rejects those defects by name, while page-build identity checks still pass because they observe identity rather than behavior. The report counts thirty-eight corpus cases, seven controlled laws with applicable examples, and twenty-four naming and twenty-one lifecycle rows inspected rather than executed.

limits.text: Refund coverage rests on the four accepted cases that pay, with the ada rows adding a destination-named control. The gate fails if the corpus stops exporting a refund case. Mint expectations come from the transcription's delta table, supported by end-state and evidence checks rather than re-proved here. Fold, keyed-mint and transaction rows are inspected as exported evidence rather than executed, and transaction wire bytes are not re-derived. The implementation handoff was local-only; publication and acceptance are separate steps.
